title: More ships attacked in Persian Gulf, oil prices rebound slightly after post-midterm plunge
content_md:
*Follow . See earlier developments below.*

#### What to know about the Iran war:

- Oil prices fell sharply after the midterm elections, as markets appeared to hope the results might push President Trump toward a deal to end and reopen the Strait of Hormuz. Commercial ships in the region continue coming under attack, however, and hitting sea mines, according to Iranian authorities.
- As a senior Iranian security official met Thursday with Russian President Vladimir Putin at the Kremlin amid uncertainty over Mr. Trump's next move, Moscow warned Russian citizens not to visit Iran, citing the "risk of a new escalation."
- Oman said Thursday it was still in talks with Iran aimed at creating a system for the nations to jointly control traffic through the vital shipping lanes of the strait, which the Omani foreign ministry said could "end the state of war and prevent renewed confrontations in the region."

#### Saudis say coalition intercepted 2 missiles launched by Houthis

The Saudi-led coalition said on social media Friday that its air defense systems intercepted and destroyed two ballistic missiles launched by Houthi rebels toward Najran, a major city in southwestern Saudi Arabia.

"Debris fell as a result of the interception, and damage assessment is underway," the statement said.

#### Iran says 2 tankers hit mines, caught fire in and near Strait of Hormuz

Iran's Revolutionary Guards said in a statement carried by state media Friday that two oil tankers hit mines and caught fire in and near the Strait of Hormuz, a day after Tehran claimed five other tankers had met similar fates.

"Two violating oil tankers — one east of the Strait of Hormuz and the other within the Strait itself — that attempted to transit via an unauthorized route struck mines," Iran's powerful Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps said in a statement carried by state TV and the semi-official Tasnim news agency.

"These two tankers had deactivated all their navigation and identification systems. Supported by the aggressive and terrorist U.S. military, they attempted to exit the Strait of Hormuz via an unauthorized path; however, upon striking mines, they caught fire and were immobilized," the statement added.

On Thursday, Iranian media reported that five oil tankers and a tugboat caught fire in the Strait of Hormuz in similar incidents.

There has, however, been no confirmation of any of these incidents from maritime officials.

Since the outbreak of the Middle East war on Feb. 28, Tehran has sought to limit traffic through the strategic waterway, which normally carries oil that amounts to one-fifth of global consumption. In response, the U.S. imposed a blockade on Iranian ports and has escorted tankers through the strait. Ships turn off their identification and navigation systems to try to avoid being detected.

The U.S. Central Command said last month that it had helped Gulf countries export 1.5 billion barrels of oil via Hormuz since summer and recently said all mines had been cleared from the vital waterway.

*CBS/AFP*

#### Putin, Iran's security chief discuss building oil pipeline from Russia to Iran

Russian President Vladimir Putin received Iran's security chief, Mohsen Rezaei, in Moscow Thursday to discuss strengthening ties between their two countries, including a pipeline to import Russian gas.

Speaking to journalists after their meeting, Rezaei, secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, called it "an extremely important exchange," according to remarks reported by the Iranian embassy.

"During the meeting with Mr. Vladimir Putin, discussions were held regarding the construction of gas pipelines from Russia to Iran," said Rezaei, Iranian state TV reported.

He noted the aim was to enable Iran "to address its own gas shortages while also facilitating the sale of Russian gas to neighbouring countries."

While a major producer, Iran has long suffered shortages of natural gas, essential for powering heating systems, which have been exacerbated by the war with the United States and Israel.

During the most intense phase of the fighting, which lasted nearly 40 days, the U.S. and Israel struck key Iranian infrastructure including natural gas refineries, according to Tehran.

#### Iranian foreign minister talks to counterparts from several Middle East countries

Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi spent much of the day on calls with his counterparts from several Middle Eastern countries, including Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates and Turkey.

In total, Araghchi held calls with nine different countries in the Middle East. Few details were shared about what was discussed on the calls, simply nodding to "diplomatic efforts to maintain stability in the region."

Notably, Pakistan was one of those countries involved as they have been very closely involved as mediators in U.S.-Iran peace talks. Araghchi spoke to their foreign minister, Ishaq Dar, on Thursday evening.

Araghchi also spoke to Saudi foreign ministers Faisal bin Farhan and Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman, despite accusations of Iranian involvement in attacks on that country by the Houthi militia in Yemen.

#### Trump administration held talks with Iran on deporting Iranians during the war, AP reports

President Trump's administration held secret talks with Iran on deporting Iranians even as the war there dragged on, court documents obtained by The Associated Press show.

The court documents unsealed Thursday show the Republican administration as recently as mid-October said it had plans to deport the Iranians through an unnamed third country, although it was unclear when it intended to do so. The judge in the case ordered the government to give the court 24-hour notice of any finalized plans to deport Iranians to Iran or to any other country and five days' written notice before any such deportation is carried out.

The documents show the administration maintained contacts with Iranian officials during the war over the removals, specifically for submitting travel documents and figuring out "possible avenues for removal."

"We are at war with a country where the President of the United States has said, as recently as two or three days ago, if not yesterday, that it is essentially lawless ... A country that is an enemy of the United States, according to the current president. A country that, according to our president, murdered tens of thousands of protestors," Judge Ana Reyes said according to the Oct. 15 transcript.

"And what you're telling me is that the United States of America is going to send individuals back to that region, facing what you and I and everyone who would ever look at this would know would be, at a minimum, a serious threat of certain death."

"Yes, your honor," Justice Department attorney Dimitar Georgiev-Remmel said. "The government is executing lawful orders of removal."

The Department of Homeland Security did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

#### Houthi drone disrupts traffic at Saudi airport, group says

The Houthis took credit for disrupting travel using a drone at King Fahd International Airport on Thursday.

"We targeted King Fahd International Airport in Dammam using a drone and our operation caused a disruption of air navigation at the airport," Houthi spokesperson Yahya Saree said on X.

The city of Dammam, which is located in the oil-rich eastern part of Saudi Arabia, and King Fahd airport have been regular targets for Houthi attacks. Multiple drones have disrupted traffic at the airport this week, according to past announcements.

Two people were killed in a Houthi strike on King Fahd airport on Oct. 22.

#### 3rd U.S. aircraft carrier strike group heading for Mideast to make stop in Singapore, delaying arrival

The USS Theodore Roosevelt aircraft carrier and its associated strike group will make a port call in Singapore Friday and will not reach the Middle East for at least another two weeks, a U.S. official told CBS News on Thursday.

There are already two carrier strike groups in the region and, which officials say is sufficient firepower to execute any commands issued by President Trump.

Mr. Trump has not signaled yet, in the wake of the U.S. midterm elections, whether he intends to order major new strikes on Iran — an option he kept on the table with repeated statements ahead of Tuesday's voting.

#### Oil prices rebound slightly after huge drop in wake of U.S. midterm elections

The initial knee-jerk reaction to the U.S. midterm election results faded a bit Thursday.

The price of a barrel of Brent crude oil, considered the international standard, rose 2.2% to $96.70, recovering a chunk of its nearly 9% drop from the day before.

Uncertainty still reigns about what will happen in the war with Iran and when the global energy industry can return to normal.

*CBS/AP*

#### As top Iranian official meets Putin, Russia warns citizens not to visit Iran, citing "risk of a new escalation"

Mohsen Rezaei, Secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, met Thursday in Moscow with Russian President Vladimir Putin to deliver a message from Iran's supreme leader, according to the Iranian government.

They met amid uncertainty over President Trump's next move on Iran in the wake of U.S. midterm election results that represented a major rebuke of his policies, including, he has admitted, the decision to launch the war with Iran alongside Israel more than eight months ago.

Mr. Trump said repeatedly ahead of the Tuesday vote that he had yet to make a decision on whether to order major new attacks on Iran or to agree a deal to end the war, which Tehran has so far refused to do until the U.S. accepts its core demands to end its naval blockade, ensure a halt to fighting on all fronts in the Middle East, and ease sanctions.

During the Rezaei-Putin meeting in Moscow on Thursday, the Russian Foreign Ministry warned Russian citizens against all travel to Iran.

"Given the continued risk of a new escalation around Iran, our recommendations to Russian citizens remain unchanged," ministry spokeswoman Maria Zakharova told reporters in Moscow. "We recommend temporarily refraining from traveling to that country until the situation is resolved. We also ask our compatriots already in Iran to exercise vigilance and avoid crowds, public events, and areas near military and government facilities."

She said the guidance was "based on the official information disseminated by Tehran," without providing any further detail.

#### Iran again claims it has no role in backing the Houthis in Yemen's civil war

The Iranian Foreign Ministry renewed the regime's rejection on Thursday of longtime and widely held beliefs that Tehran materially supports the Houthi rebels fighting the Saudi Arabia-backed government in Yemen's decade-long civil war. The conflict intensified a couple months ago and quickly became the most active and deadly front in the intertwined conflicts in the Middle East.

Foreign ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei called the latest accusation of Iranian support for the Houthis, made Monday by European Union foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas, "baseless," and said Iran "strongly denied claims that Iranian military experts were present in Yemen."

The U.S. government, along with many other Western nations and the NATO alliance, have demanded for years that Iran stop supporting the Houthis. The support, according to these nations, includes financial backing, weapons and other equipment, and direct coordination and training.

In July, not long before the Yemen war escalated and the Houthis started launching attacks on Saudi airports in response, the Reuters news agency reported that Iran had flown commanders from its powerful, heavily sanctioned Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, along with equipment related to missiles and drones, to Yemen bolster the Houthis' ability to threaten global energy supplies in the Red Sea.

Since then, have killed at least 20 people.

In her remarks Monday, the EU's Kallas said "all Houthi military action must end immediately. We call on all actors, including Iran to cease all military support to the Houthis, in violation of several United Nations Security Council resolutions."

Iran has always denied supporting the Houthis.

#### Oman says still working with Iran on joint control system for Strait of Hormuz "that would end the state of war"

Oman's government said Thursday that, in a phone call between the Omani and Iranian foreign ministers, both men "stressed the importance of moving from the stage of de-escalating tensions to one of establishing sustainable understandings based on practical arrangements to ensure the safety of maritime routes and joint technical mechanisms to secure the smooth flow of international trade and energy, in a manner that would end the state of war and prevent renewed confrontations in the region."

Omani Foreign Minister Sayyid Badr bin Hamad bin Hamoud Al Busaidi and his Iranian counterpart Abbas Araghchi "reviewed the latest developments in communications and discussions aimed at reaching practical, political, and technical understandings that would enable the resumption of unimpeded maritime traffic through the Strait of Hormuz," the Omani Foreign Ministry said in a statement.

Iran and Oman have discussed for months implementing a joint mechanism to control commercial traffic through the strait, over which both Iran and the U.S. insist they currently have dominion. Iran started threatening and attacking ships in the region in response to the U.S. and Israel jointly launching the ongoing war against the Islamic Republic at the end of February, and those attacks continue despite U.S. assertions that the strait is now open safe to use.

According to Oman, the ministers emphasized in their Thursday call that any future "understandings must be based on respect for the sovereignty of states, consideration of the legitimate interests of all parties, and the creation of appropriate conditions for restoring dialogue and negotiation processes and addressing the outstanding issues underlying the escalation."

#### Another oil tanker hits mine, catches fire near Strait of Hormuz, Iran says

An oil tanker hit a mine, caught fire and was immobilized east of the Strait of Hormuz early on Thursday, Iran's Revolutionary Guard Corp navy said, according to IRNA, Tehran's official news agency.

The navy said the tanker had switched off its identification and navigation systems, a tactic used by vessels seeking to avoid detection by Iran.

The IRGC has declared the strait "unsafe and closed" to vessels trying to go through the vital waterway without coordination with Tehran.

#### Saudi coalition says it intercepted Houthi missile fired at Medina region

The Saudi-led coalition fighting Yemen's Houthi rebels said on Thursday that a ballistic missile fired by the group at the Medina region — home to one of Islam's holiest cities — had been intercepted.

"Air defense intercepted and destroyed a ballistic missile launched by the terrorist Houthi militia toward the Medina region," coalition spokesman Turki al-Malki said in a social media post.

#### Tanker hit by 2 projectiles north of Qatar, British military says

A tanker was hit by two unidentified projectiles in the Persian Gulf about 50 nautical miles north of Madinat ash Shamal, Qatar, a British military tracking agency said Thursday.

The United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations Centre (KKMTO) said the status of the crew, damage assessment and environmental impact weren't known.

#### Iran says two tankers and tugboat caught fire in Strait of Hormuz

Two oil tankers and a tugboat caught fire in the Strait of Hormuz, Iran's Revolutionary Guard Corps said, local media reported on Thursday.

Since the outbreak of the Iran war on Feb. 28, Tehran has severely restricted traffic through the strategic waterway, which normally carries about one-fifth of global oil consumption.

In response, the United States has imposed a blockade on Iranian ports and helped tankers travel through the strait. The U.S. Central Command said last month that it had helped Gulf countries export 1.5 billion barrels of oil via the strait since summer.

"Last night, in two separate incidents, a large oil tanker attempting to pass through the illegal passageway south of the Strait of Hormuz suffered a fire after striking a mine and was brought to a halt," the Guard told Iran's Fars news agency.

"Another supertanker was halted by a massive fire while exiting the eastern Strait of Hormuz. A tugboat that had approached the supertanker to extinguish the fire also caught fire."

Fars also reported the IRGC navy's electronic warfare unit had taken control of two LUCAS drones, a U.S.-developed model short for Low-cost Uncrewed Combat Attack System.

#### Reelected Colorado Rep. Jason Crow on Iran after midterms: "The war has got to end"

Colorado Democratic Rep. Jason Crow, who has won his midterm reelection bid, told CBS News how Democrats will address the war with Iran as the party takes control of Congress next year, saying, "The war has got to end."

"Americans never wanted it to begin with. Americans for years have wanted to end this constant cycle of conflict in the Middle East. In fact, Donald Trump even campaigned on that," Crow, a member of the House Armed Services Committee, told Major Garrett on "The Takeout" on Wednesday night.

Asked whether Congress plans to address the war through war power resolutions or

using the power of appropriations to take away funding, Crow replied: "Yes."

"We have voted on seven resolutions and passed two of them so far. We should continue to take votes. Let people stand up," he added. "Appropriations is one of our most powerful tools. We have to be willing to do that too."

When it comes to the future of Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, Crow said that future "should be short."

"Pete Hegseth is incompetent. He was never qualified to do this, never should have been in the position to begin with. He needs to go," he said.

#### U.S. sanctions Indian companies over alleged maritime fraud aiding Iran

The United States on Wednesday issued sanctions targeting what it described as a "vast criminal network" run by two Indian nationals that was aiding Iran's shadow fleet of oil tankers in committing maritime fraud.

In a statement, the U.S. Treasury said the network aided Iranian vessels in sailing under false flags and in gaining fake maritime certifications.

The move was the latest in a tightening web of U.S. sanctions targeting Iran since August, when Washington announced it would be seeking the "economic asphyxiation" of the country in conjunction with its military campaign.

"As we have said many times, under Operation Economic Outcast, you are either with us or against us," said Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, who has in the past threatened sanctions against any country or company that aids Iran, regardless of its relationship with Washington.

Wednesday's sanctions named Indian nationals Suniel Kumar Sharma and his wife Jaspreet Preeti Shahid as operating a large-scale maritime fraud network from their base in Chandigarh.

"Purporting to represent nations from nearly every continent, from Guyana to Eswatini and Laos, Sharma and Shahid have allowed the Iranian shadow fleet ... to evade international restrictions on their operation," the Treasury said in a statement.

#### Head of Iran's Supreme National Security Council takes shot at U.S. in wake of election

The powerful head of the Iranian Supreme National Security Council gave credit to his country for the rebuke of President Trump in the midterm elections.

"The Iranian nation handed Trump a strategic defeat on the battlefield and in the Hormuz — and a POLITICAL DEFEAT in Washington," Mohsen Rezaei said on X. "Meanwhile, Americans got stuck with the bill for his war."

"Anyone who takes on Iran will pay the price — from the battlefield to their own doorstep," he added.

Vice President JD Vance reportedly reached out to Rezaei last week about discussing conditions for a ceasefire and negotiations on the war. It's unclear how the midterm elections will affect Iran's negotiations to end the war, but President Trump said he did not regret the attacks.

#### Following Democratic wave, Schumer says war in Iran "must end"

Top Senate Democrat Chuck Schumer said Wednesday that the Iran war "must end" and suggested his party's incoming majority in Congress could use their control over government funding to press for that goal.

"The American people don't know what the heck we're fighting for in Iran," Schumer told journalists. "He's never made it clear he changes his mind day to day and minute to minute. This war must end. It must end."

He later noted the "power of the purse" is "one of the ways of deterring a president who does war without the consent of the American people."

Schumer and Democrats in Congress have been pushing to pass war powers resolutions throughout the war. The bills would force President Trump to remove soldiers from Iran.

The longtime New York Democrat also intimated funding could be pulled in order to force the war to come to an end.

Exit polls most think the U.S. made the wrong decision to take that military action, including about a quarter of Republicans.

*AFP/CBS*

#### Trump says it's "largely true" the war in Iran cost Republicans in midterms

President Trump said it's "probably true" the war in Iran was responsible in the midterm elections, specifically the cost of gas related to the war.

"Well, I think it's largely true because it drove the gasoline up a little bit short term," he told reporters at an event related to the ballroom's construction. "But at the same time, if I had it to do again, I'd have to do it again. Because long term, it's the only answer. You can't let Iran have a nuclear weapon."

Mr. Trump was responding to a question about Vice President JD Vance on the war in a post on X earlier in the day.

"But I can tell you that as far as that war is concerned, I would have done nothing different," Trump continued. "We've totally broken their military. The navy's gone. Their air force is gone. Their anti-aircraft is gone."

#### Red Cross delivers first supplies to Yemen's Taiz in over a month

The International Committee of the Red Cross said it delivered medical supplies into Taiz on Wednesday for the first time in weeks since the Iran-backed Houthis surrounded the Yemeni city.

The ICRC "delivered four trucks of essential medical supplies to Taiz city, including surgical kits to help hospitals treat weapon-wounded patients," it said in a statement. "This is the ICRC's first delivery of medical supplies to hospitals in Taiz City since 23 September, just before the intensification of fighting in the area."

Taiz, which is located in western Yemen, has become the focal point of the war between the Iran-backed Houthis and Saudi-backed Yemeni army. In late summer, the Houthis swept through the western part of the country and acquired wide swaths of land up to the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, which forms the southern opening to the Red Sea.

Taiz, the country's third-largest city, was left isolated from international aid groups when the Houthis rapidly took over the territory.

#### Brent crude drops under $100, lowest level since September

Brent crude oil, the international standard, dropped significantly on Wednesday, falling under $100 a barrel for the first time since September.

The price was down over 8% at noon Eastern time, falling to about $94 a barrel. The cost hasn't been under $95 a barrel since Sept. 1.

Brent crude last closed at under $100 a barrel on Sept. 30. The cost then consistently rose to a high of $116 per barrel on Oct. 23. It has dropped since, closing at $103 per barrel on Tuesday.

The decrease comes a day after Democrats won by a landslide in midterm elections, rebuking President Trump and his position on the war with Iran. Democrats, who have already voted several times in the House to restore war powers to Congress, are likely to pursue de-escalation in the conflict.

#### Trump asking advisers if Pete Hegseth should go, sources say

President Trump has been asking advisers around him and on the phone whether Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth should stay in his job, following Republicans' catastrophic losses Tuesday night, multiple sources familiar with the matter tell CBS News.

Some White House aides have predicted some of the blame for GOP midterm losses will be trained on Adm. Brad Cooper, the head of U.S. Central Command, and Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff Gen. Dan Caine, who both played big roles in guidance on the Iran war.

Still, other sources said the president hasn't decided to replace Hegseth. Before the election, Democrats were already trying to impeach Hegseth, and the likelihood of an impeachment effort could increase with Democrats holding strong majorities in both chambers.

.

#### Vance blames Iran conflict for GOP midterm defeats: "The reason we lost is the war"

In his first public comments on the election results, Vice President JD Vance said the reason Republicans were handedly defeated in the House and Senate is because of the war in Iran.

"The reason we lost is the war. The president himself said so last night," Vance wrote in a post on X. "If you'd like to argue it was worth it, that losing the Senate for the next 6 years was worth it, then do so. Argue it was a worthwhile cost to pay. Agree or disagree, that's at least honest. But everyone knows why we lost. And any honest conversation about where we go from here must start there."

The vice president, a possible 2028 contender, said many voters who backed the Trump-Vance ticket in 2024 cast their ballots for Democrats in 2026 for four reasons: to end the war with Iran, focus on the cost of living and inflation, put America first and change the U.S. relationship with Israel.

"Our voters showed up," Vance wrote. "And the above four reasons are why many of them voted for Democrats."

#### Iran claims to have shot down another U.S. MQ-1 drone over island in Strait of Hormuz

Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps said in a statement Wednesday it had shot down a U.S. MQ-1 drone over Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz, claiming it was the 15th of the type downed by Iranian forces during the war.

In September, U.S. officials told CBS News on condition of anonymity that Iranian forces had, at that time, brought down at least two MQ-1s.

The U.S. military has fielded two principal MQ-1 variants: the Predator, which became a fixture of U.S. operations in Iraq and Afghanistan before the Air Force retired it in 2018, and the Gray Eagle, a larger Predator-derived aircraft still operated by the Army, including its special operations forces.

Both the Predator and Gray Eagle were designed for intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance missions but they can also carry Hellfire missiles for striking targets. In the Strait of Hormuz, these unmanned aircraft can provide U.S. forces with persistent surveillance over the narrow waterway while also tracking Iranian military activity and monitoring threats to both American forces and commercial shipping.

The Air Force's older MQ-1 Predators have largely been retired, but if Iran has in fact shot down 10 of the aircraft, the loss would still equate to roughly $40 million.

#### Houthis claim to have struck Saudi Arabian capital's King Khalid airport again with ballistic missile

Iran's Houthi allies in Yemen claimed Wednesday to have struck King Khalid International Airport in the Saudi Arabian capital Riyadh with a ballistic missile, causing "extensive damage."

Saudi Arabia, despite its significant size, wealth and military advantage over the Iran-backed Yemeni rebels, by the group. Previous Houthi strikes on Saudi airports in October killed at least 20 people, most of them at King Khalid.

In a statement shared Wednesday on social media, Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree warned that the the Riyadh airport was "unsafe" and he renewed the group's "call to all international airlines, employees, and travelers not to travel through Saudi airspace, as it is unsafe, with the exception of the airspace over the holy areas of Mecca and Medina."

There was no immediate comment from Saudi authorities on the Houthi claim to have hit the airport again on Wednesday.

#### Houthis claim series of successful attacks on Saudi Arabian forces

The Iran-backed Houthis in Yemen claimed Wednesday to have shot down a Chinese-made armed reconnaissance drone operated by Saudi Arabia over Yemen's southern Taiz province.

In a statement shared online by Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree said it was the 10th Saudi operated drone of the type downed by the rebels during the current escalation of Yemen's civil war, in which Saudi Arabia backs the Yemeni government.

Saree said in a string of social media posts that the Houthis had also "carried out an operation targeting Saudi enemy forces" with six ballistic missiles east of Yemen's al-Jawf province, "leaving dozens dead and wounded and destroying a number of military vehicles."

Other Houthi operations targeted a radar installation north of Jizan, Saudi Arabia, and a Saudi military encampment in Najran, he said.

There was no immediate comment from Saudi authorities on the Houthi claims.

#### Iranians take to streets of Tehran for pro-regime rally

People marched through central Tehran Wednesday in a major pro-regime rally to mark the 47th anniversary of the 1979 takeover of the U.S. embassy in the Iranian capital, chanting anti-U.S. and Israel slogans.

Some held signs calling for revenge for the killing of former Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei at the outset of the ongoing war, while others mocked President Trump.

"We are not happy about the surge in oil prices," said one woman, who gave AFP only her last name, Mahmoudkhani.

"But there is some satisfaction in knowing we are no longer living this torment alone. We, alone, have been suffering under sanctions for so many years," she added.

Some echoed Iranian officials doubts' that the election results would change much for Iranians.

"Whether it is the Democrats or the Republicans, there is no difference for us," Mohammad, a 42-year-old civil servant, told AFP. "The US government's approach toward the Iranian people has unfortunately remained the same over the past 50 years."

#### Statement attributed to Iran's supreme leader plays down hopes of shift in U.S. war policy

A statement attributed to Iran's elusive Supreme Leader Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei on Wednesday said anyone expecting a shift in U.S. policy regarding the war with Iran in the wake of the American midterm elections was "seriously mistaken."

"Those who still harbor even the slightest hope that the behavior of the hegemonic system might change through partisan or factional shifts, or who imagine that making concessions to the United States can dissuade it from hostility towards the Iranian nation, are seriously mistaken," said the statement published on Khamenei's website.

Khamenei was named as the successor to his father, former leader Ali Khamenei, soon after the older man was killed in the initial wave of U.S.-Israeli strikes at the outset of the war. U.S. officials believe the younger Khamenei was seriously wounded in the same strike, and he has not been seen or heard from directly at all since being named the new supreme leader.

President Trump has said the war with Iran was partly responsible for the dismal midterm election results for his Republican party this week, but that he does not regret his decision to launch it in conjunction with Israel.

In the message released Wednesday, Khamenei warned that "should such aggressions be repeated, the war's scope will become much wider."

#### Trump says U.S. has no immediate plan to strike Iran, despite being "locked and loaded"

President Trump told the Financial Times newspaper on Tuesday evening that he had no immediate plans to order new strikes on Iran, after keeping the option on the table for weeks ahead of the U.S. midterm elections.

"We seem to be getting everything we want," the FT quoted Mr. Trump as saying, referring to the current stalemate with Iran. While major fighting stopped weeks ago, the standoff has seen the Islamic Republic continue threatening and attacking commercial ships in the Strait of Hormuz, which in turn has kept global oil prices 60% to 70% higher than they were before the war started, driving up consumer costs across the globe.

Asked whether there would be a new attack on Iran later this week, Mr. Trump said "we're locked and loaded if we need to go, but there may be no reason for it."

Despite the impasse, the president claimed the current circumstances were "brilliant," with oil still reaching global markets from the Persian Gulf, including under U.S. military escort through the Strait of Hormuz.

"If you think about it, we haven't really had a war with them in a long time. Six months, maybe more," asserted Mr. Trump.

#### China says avoiding more conflict in Middle East a "top priority"

China's foreign ministry said Wednesday that avoiding a resumption of the conflict between Iran and the U.S. was a "top priority" in its diplomatic efforts in the region.

"The top priority is to avoid the resumption of hostilities in the Middle East that would bring disaster to the region's people," Chinese Foreign Ministry spokeswoman Mao Ning told reporters in Beijing.

China will "support Iran and the U.S. in resolving disputes through negotiations, promote finding a political settlement to the Yemen issue, to help reach a proper and comprehensive solution for the opening of the Strait of Hormuz," she added.

China is an economic ally of Iran. Chinese purchases of Iranian crude oil amount to nearly 45% of the Iranian government's budget, according to a U.S. government report from March 2025.

Later this month, Beijing will send its Middle East envoy to Iran, Oman and Saudi Arabia for visits "aimed at promoting peace talks (and) easing tensions," the foreign ministry said Wednesday.

#### Lebanese prime minister warns of "risks of renewed war," and of Lebanon being dragged in again

In a message seemingly directed at the Iran-backed group Hezbollah, Lebanon's prime minister warned Wednesday against any moves that could pull the country into renewed fighting between Iran and the U.S. and Israel.

"Faced with the risks of renewed war in the region, I renew my warning of the dangers of dragging Lebanon into a new senseless adventure in service of outside interests," Nawaf Salam said on Wednesday, without explicitly mentioning Hezbollah.

Southern Lebanon has been a major front in the interlinked regional conflicts, with fighting between Iran's Hezbollah allies and Israel's military driving tens of thousands of people from their homes and killing almost 9,000 since Oct. 7, 2023, according to the Lebanese health ministry.

Hezbollah, long a powerful political and paramilitary force in the country, pulled Lebanon directly into the war with Israel by launching strikes on the Jewish state in support of Hamas after the 2023 terror attacks sparked the war in Gaza, and then by firing rockets and missiles in support of Iran after joint U.S.-Israeli strikes commenced on Feb. 28.

The Lebanon conflict has proven to be a major sticking point in negotiations between the U.S. and Iran, as Tehran has consistently rejected any peace deal with Washington that does not also end fighting in Lebanon and Gaza.

A fragile ceasefire agreement reached between Israel and Hezbollah in June has halted most large-scale fighting between the two sides, but Israeli forces still occupy a large section of southern Lebanon, and there are sporadic attacks by both sides.

"We do not accept the country again becoming a theater for the conflict of others," Salam added, saying Lebanon had "already paid a heavy price."

President Trump threatened repeatedly ahead of the U.S. midterm elections to renew strikes on Iran, but he told the Financial Times as the results came in Tuesday evening that he had no immediate plans to order attacks.

#### Four tankers catch fire while transiting Strait of Hormuz, Iran's military says

Four oil tankers caught fire after hitting mines while attempting to pass through the Strait of Hormuz, Iran's military said Wednesday, after it warned no one would benefit from a return to war.

"Four non-compliant oil tankers attempting to pass through the prohibited passage south of the Strait of Hormuz were destroyed after striking naval mines and are still burning," Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guards Corps said in a statement quoted by state TV.

"Two other non-compliant ships or vessels have also been halted," they said

The attacks come even as a diplomatic push is underway aimed at reaching a deal between the U.S. and Iran. Indirect talks via Qatari, Pakistani and Saudi mediators are understood to be underway.

Although both sides previously expressed some hope of reaching an agreement, Iran's Secretary of the Supreme National Security Council on Tuesday cast doubt on progress toward a deal, calling the U.S. response to their demands "not convincing."

#### Iran says midterm results reflect rejection of war

Iran's chief negotiator said Wednesday the midterm election results mean Americans have rejected the war with his country.

"Americans said NO TO WAR, and we endorse this message," Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf said in a post on X.

He cited the increased cost of living or "conscience" as two of the possible reasons for the widespread Republican losses in Tuesday's vote.

"If the U.S. govt betrays their public will to serve international paymasters and blackmailers, it will learn our NO comes with a Nightmare," Ghalibaf added.

#### Trump acknowledges war with Iran partially to blame for GOP's election defeat

President Trump acknowledged on Tuesday night that the war with Iran was partially responsible for the Republicans' defeat in the midterm elections.

In a phone interview with Fox News, Mr. Trump said "part of it was Iran" when explaining the result of the elections, but that "at the same time, people understand the importance of what I've done."

In a separate interview with the The Wall Street Journal, the president reiterated his comments and added that he does not regret starting the war with Tehran.

"I don't think about it. I did the right thing. I would have done it again," he told the newspaper.

#### Qatar is said to expect feedback from U.S. and Iran on latest peace proposal within 36 hours

Qatari mediators expect feedback within 36 hours from Iranian and U.S. negotiators on new ideas aimed at getting both sides closer to a deal to end the war, Reuters reported Tuesday, citing an official briefed on the talks.

"The mediators came up with a new suggestion to move the process along, and it's currently being studied by the two sides," the official told Reuters.

Efforts to reach a deal to prevent a return to fighting between Iran and the U.S. have ramped up recently. President Trump has said he is still open to an agreement, but has also threatened to resume major U.S. strikes after Tuesday's midterm elections in the U.S.

On the eve of the elections, Mr. Trump again expressed hope that an agreement could still be reached, claiming Tehran wanted a settlement "as soon as possible."

Iranian officials declared Monday that the ball "is in the U.S. court" and they said Iran's core demands to end the war would not be altered.
topic: Tàu bị tấn công ở vịnh Ba Tư, giá dầu hồi nhẹ
summary: Giá dầu Brent tăng 2,2% lên 96,70 USD/thùng vào thứ Năm, phục hồi một phần mức giảm gần 9% của ngày hôm trước sau cuộc bầu cử giữa kỳ Mỹ.
Brent giảm xuống dưới 100 USD/thùng lần đầu tiên kể từ tháng 9 vào thứ Tư, giảm hơn 8% xuống khoảng 94 USD; đỉnh là 116 USD/thùng ngày 23/10 và đóng cửa 103 USD ngày thứ Ba.

Vệ binh Cách mạng Hồi giáo Iran (IRGC) cho biết hai tàu chở dầu trúng mìn và bốc cháy trong và gần eo biển Hormuz vào thứ Sáu, một ngày sau khi Tehran nói năm tàu chở dầu khác gặp tình huống tương tự; chưa có xác nhận từ phía hàng hải.
Liên minh do Saudi Arabia dẫn đầu cho biết đã đánh chặn hai tên lửa đạn đạo của Houthi nhắm vào Najran và một tên lửa nhắm vào khu vực Medina.
Oman cho biết vẫn đàm phán với Iran về cơ chế chung kiểm soát giao thông qua eo biển Hormuz; Nga khuyến cáo công dân không đến Iran vì rủi ro leo thang mới.

Mỹ trừng phạt mạng lưới do hai công dân Ấn Độ điều hành, bị cho là giúp đội tàu dầu ngầm của Iran gian lận hàng hải; theo CBS, tàu sân bay USS Theodore Roosevelt sẽ ghé Singapore và chưa tới Trung Đông trong ít nhất hai tuần.
analysis: Nhận định: Theo bài, Brent tăng 2,2% lên 96,70 USD/thùng sau cú giảm gần 9%, vì tàu bị tấn công ở Hormuz. Giá dầu còn biến động mạnh nên có thể tác động tới lạm phát, chi phí vận tải và tâm lý thị trường. Ngân hàng nên theo dõi chất lượng tín dụng ngành dầu khí, vận tải, hàng không.

title: Democratic sweep gives markets a reason to rethink path of interest rates
content_md:
The Democrats' resounding victory in the U.S. midterms has the potential to curb interest rate hikes globally next year, according to market watchers — but the uncertain path of oil prices, U.S. economic growth and fiscal policies will be key.

Central banks around the world are back in monetary tightening mode, with the Federal Reserve, Bank of England, European Central Bank and Bank of Japan all raising rates in recent months.

The shift has in part stemmed from the U.S. and Israel's war with Iran driving up prices in oil and gas markets. The war has also exacerbated a squeeze in global refining capacity which has sent the cost of products like diesel, gasoline and jet fuel soaring.

Traders largely expected big Democratic gains this week after polls pointed in their favor, but there was still uncertainty leading up to the vote about whether the party would capture both chambers of Congress, increasing the ability for lawmakers to challenge President Donald Trump's policymaking.

Crude oil prices tumbled following the clear-cut Democratic victory in both the House and Senate, with international benchmark ICE Brent crude falling 8.7% on Wednesday, closing below $100 a barrel for the first time since September.

That was largely attributed to raised expectations that the result may mean Trump is more inclined to strike a deal to end the war in Iran, helping restore Gulf refinery capacity and improve export conditions. Vice President JD Vance's lengthy statement blaming Republican losses on the Iran war boosted that view.

Dan Coatsworth, head of markets at AJ Bell, said there had been "an admission from the Republican camp that the Iran war cost them a clean sweep in the election, which the market has taken to indicate that a swift resolution to the Middle East conflict could help them save face."

"Trump might relish the opportunity to take all the credit if an end to the war leads to a big drop in energy costs."

If the election result "pushes for a resolution of the conflict in the Middle East, that might bring oil down, and that's been an issue for the Fed and inflation, and part of the reason why rates are higher," said Andrew Slimmon, senior portfolio manager and head of the Applied Equity Advisors at Morgan Stanley.

Historic data shows a tight correlation between oil prices and global rates, Ralph Axel, rates strategist at Bank of America, said in a research note published Thursday. Higher oil prices over the next three to six months would likely mean "significantly higher interest rates" in the U.S., but especially so in the U.K. and Germany, he said.

"If oil prices rise, we think rates will too, especially at the front end where long-end term premium is less of a factor and monetary policy expectations play a larger role," he added.

As the uptick in crude prices on Thursday and choppiness on Friday showed, a resolution to the nearly nine-month-long conflict is far from locked in.

"For now, oil has begun to climb back up again, and interest rate expectations have not radically changed from pre-election levels," AJ Bell's Dan Coatsworth noted.

Money markets on Thursday indicated a moderate change in expectations from a week ago, both in the U.S. and Europe, with traders pricing in a slightly higher chance of monetary easing on a one-year horizon.

The effect on a two-year timeframe was more pronounced in the euro area than the U.S., according to CNBC analysis of LSEG data, with rate pricing down 8.7 basis points on the week for the ECB versus 4.6 basis points for the Fed.

"Republicans don't really have an off-ramp here at this stage," said Laurel Rapp, director for the U.S. and North America Program at Chatham House. "We know the Democrats will seek to take votes in the House and the Senate to constrain the Republicans, to restrain the administration on Iran war powers. But whether that will bind the administration is another matter."

Eurasia Group's Clayton Allen meanwhile told CNBC's "Squawk Box Asia" that while the war with Iran is unpopular at home, leaving the Middle East region without tangible wins would also be unpopular and that he expected an escalation within weeks.

Andrew Bailey, governor of the Bank of England — which hiked rates by 25 basis points on Thursday — told CNBC that energy price pressures stemmed from a combination of obstructions on the Strait of Hormuz, a shortage in refining capacity, and low European gas storage.

"A peace process in the Middle East will not shift all of those elements," he told CNBC's Steve Sedgwick on Thursday.

"Let's wait and see, because we have seen that fall in energy prices over the last 48 hours, but it is a very volatile situation, as we've learnt over the last seven, eight, nine months."

Ken Egan, head of European Sovereign Credit at KBRA, said the interest rate outlook would be primarily impacted by whether economies have enough underlying momentum for existing inflation pressures to become more persistent.

Europe is "heading into winter after months of elevated energy prices, and the full impact is still feeding through to the wider economy," he said by email.

"The concern for central banks is whether these pressures start to push up wages and prices more broadly, or whether weaker demand limits that pass-through."

A key question for the Federal Reserve will be whether the blue sweep "could lead to more fiscal prudence in the U.S. and thus less inflation," Jane Foley, head of FX strategy at Rabobank, said by email.

"It is very early, however, to be sure of the fiscal outlook, not least because many Democrats were voted in to soften cost of living pressures ... so it is very difficult to come to a firm conclusion at this point as to how the outlook for rates will change next year," she said.

The high level of U.S. fiscal stimulus and whether it is about to change is the "million dollar question" right now, James Sullivan, managing director and head of Asia Pacific equity research at J.P. Morgan, told CNBC's "Squawk Box Asia."

"The reasons why you're seeing inflation running high is a combination of a range of factors, from the war in Iran, to tariffs, to significant tightness in particular areas of the energy complex," he said.

"But it's also important to recognize the U.S. government has continued to spend at very high levels, into an economic expansion with low unemployment, and that's driving very specific macroeconomic implications. If that changes, you potentially take the pressure off the rate environment in a way that gives the Fed significantly more forward flexibility."

Daniel Clifton, head of policy research at Baird Strategas, said the impact on the data center buildout in the U.S. was another big factor to watch.

"In 2025, we had major fiscal headwinds, and it really didn't matter because we had such a big capex boom in the AI build-out last year. This year was driven a lot by stimulus," he told CNBC's "Squawk Box Europe."

"If you have an environment where you have tighter fiscal policy — the Fed is raising rates right now — and you have a slowdown in the AI capex build out, you're probably going to reach a policy mistake at some point in mid-2027," he said.

"That's what happened in 2000 during the Y2K tech boom, the Fed was raising rates, we had higher oil prices, and they just went too far, and eventually it had a recession. Our forecast is not for a recession in the United States. Our forecast is that we'll have a mid-cycle slowdown in 2027."

summary: Rate hikes could be curbed by an Iran war resolution, slower U.S. growth and fresh fiscal policy — but none are set in stone.
analysis: Nhận định: Bài chỉ nêu lập luận rằng việc tăng lãi suất có thể được hạn chế, nhưng chưa chắc chắn. Nếu kỳ vọng lãi suất toàn cầu hạ nhiệt, áp lực lên tỷ giá và lãi suất trong nước có thể giảm. Tác động tới ngân hàng ta còn gián tiếp và chưa rõ.

title: Thiên Long về tay tập đoàn Nhật Bản
description: Tập đoàn Kokuyo của Nhật Bản vừa hoàn tất nhận 47% vốn của Thiên Long từ cổ đông lớn TLAT, trước khi chào mua công khai thêm cổ phiếu.
content_md:
Tập đoàn Kokuyo của Nhật Bản vừa hoàn tất nhận 47% vốn của Thiên Long từ cổ đông lớn TLAT, trước khi chào mua công khai thêm cổ phiếu.

Tập đoàn Thiên Long (TLG) vừa thông báo Công ty Đầu tư Thiên Long An Thịnh (TLAT) đã hoàn tất việc chuyển nhượng toàn bộ cổ phần cho Tập đoàn Kokuyo vào hôm nay, sau khi nhận được sự chấp thuận của cơ quan có thẩm quyền. TLAT là cổ đông lớn nhất của Thiên Long, sở hữu gần 45,2 triệu cổ phần, tương đương 46,82% vốn điều lệ.

Các bước tiếp theo, bao gồm việc chào mua công khai cổ phiếu TLG, sẽ được Kokuyo triển khai theo quy định. Ban lãnh đạo Thiên Long cho biết các diễn biến nêu trên không ảnh hưởng trực tiếp đến hoạt động sản xuất kinh doanh hằng ngày của TLG. Công ty tiếp tục tập trung bảo đảm chất lượng sản phẩm, tiêu chuẩn dịch vụ và hiệu quả vận hành.

Cuối năm trước, Thiên Long công bố cổ đông lớn TLAT đang đàm phán với Tập đoàn Kokuyo để chuyển nhượng toàn bộ cổ phần. Bên cạnh đó, Kokuyo dự kiến thực hiện chào mua công khai thêm 18,19% vốn TLG. Nếu thành công, tỷ lệ sở hữu của họ sẽ đạt 65,01% và đưa Thiên Long trở thành công ty con.

Thông báo mới nhất không xác nhận tổng giá trị của thương vụ. Tuy nhiên, theo công bố từ Kokuyo hồi tháng 12/2025, doanh nghiệp Nhật dự tính chi khoảng 27,6 tỷ yen (tương đương 4.700 tỷ đồng vào thời điểm đó).

Thành lập năm 1905, Kokuyo là tập đoàn hàng đầu Nhật Bản trong lĩnh vực văn phòng phẩm và giải pháp không gian làm việc. Tại Việt Nam, Kokuyo hiện kinh doanh các sản phẩm văn phòng phẩm mang thương hiệu Campus, đồng thời đã hợp tác TLG trong các hợp đồng sản xuất theo yêu cầu và thiết kế (OEM).

Nói với *VnExpress* bên lề phiên họp thường niên hồi tháng 4, ông Cô Gia Thọ, Chủ tịch Hội đồng quản trị, cho biết Kokuyo là một doanh nghiệp lâu năm, nên khi hợp tác với họ, ông cũng muốn Thiên Long có thể trở thành một thương hiệu có tuổi đời lâu dài tương tự. Hơn hết, khi xem xét các thương vụ trước đây của Kokuyo, ông Thọ thấy phong cách của họ là đầu tư nhưng vẫn tìm cách giữ vững thương hiệu địa phương, chứ không chỉ hướng tới mục đích thâu tóm thông thường.

"Một phần nào đó, tôi cũng cảm thấy an tâm khi giao Thiên Long cho một công ty như vậy", ông Thọ nói.

Tập đoàn Thiên Long thành lập năm 1981, được ông Cô Gia Thọ gầy dựng từ một xưởng sản xuất nhỏ thành doanh nghiệp đầu ngành bút viết và văn phòng phẩm. Thiên Long nổi tiếng với sản phẩm bút bi cùng tên và các thương hiệu khác như FlexOffice, Colokit và Flexio. Nhờ tham gia xuất khẩu từ sớm, sản phẩm của họ còn hiện diện trên 75 quốc gia và vùng lãnh thổ

9 tháng đầu năm, TLG ghi nhận doanh thu thuần hợp nhất khoảng 3.621 tỷ đồng, tăng 12% so với cùng kỳ. Lợi nhuận sau thuế đạt hơn 423 tỷ đồng, cải thiện khoảng 12,5%. Nguyên nhân chủ yếu đến từ sự tăng trưởng doanh thu, kết hợp với tỷ lệ lợi nhuận ròng được duy trì tương đồng so với cùng kỳ, đạt mức 11,7%.

title: MIK Group starts 50-ha high-rise residential project in northern Vietnam city
content_md:
Vietnamese property developer MIK Group has broken ground on The Harbor Skyline, a nearly 50-hectare high-rise residential development on Vu Yen island in Hai Phong, marking the debut of its I Series apartment brand in the northern port city.

The groundbreaking ceremony took place on Wednesday, and the developer has not disclosed further details on its total investment or construction schedule.

The launch also marks MIK Group's expansion into Hai Phong with its I Series, a premium apartment brand that has become a core part of the company's high-rise residential portfolio.

MIK Group develops two main apartment lines, M Series and I Series, targeting different market segments and housing needs. I Series includes projects such as Imperia Smart City, Imperia Signature Co Loa, Imperia Ocean City, Imperia Sky Park, and Imperia Sensa Park.

The line accounts for an estimated 70-80% of MIK Group's total high-rise apartment portfolio. The company has brought around 17,000 I Series apartments to market and plans to develop a further 200,000 units in the coming years.

A company representative described Hai Phong as the next step in MIK Group's expansion. The city, home to LG's Vietnam plant, is one of the region's major economic hubs, supported by industrial manufacturing, seaport operations and logistics.

**Major developers intensify competition in Hai Phong**

MIK Group's entry comes as Hai Phong's real estate market becomes increasingly crowded with large developers seeking to secure land and establish a presence across residential, commercial and resort segments.

Vingroup has established a substantial footprint through projects including the 877-hectare Vinhomes Royal Island on Vu Yen island, Vinhomes Duong Kinh, and the Happy Home Trang Cat social housing development.

Local developer Hoang Huy Group has built a strong position through projects such as Hoang Huy New City and Hoang Huy Green River in Thuy Nguyen.

DOJI Land entered the high-rise market with developments including Diamond Crown Hai Phong and Golden Crown Hai Phong, while Masterise Homes is targeting the premium apartment segment, particularly in Thuy Nguyen.

Other developers are expanding their presence through large-scale urban and resort developments. Van Phu Invest is developing the 30-hectare Vlasta Thuy Nguyen project, while Geleximco is behind the 480-hectare Dragon Ocean international tourism area in Do Son. BRG Group is developing the 350-hectare Ruby Coastal City resort township.

The growing presence of these developers reflects Hai Phong's appeal as an investment destination, supported by its industrial base, port infrastructure, and expanding urban economy.

title: Doanh nghiệp Đài Loan mở rộng hợp tác sản xuất tại Việt Nam
description: Đoàn doanh nghiệp Đài Loan (Trung Quốc) tổ chức buổi giao lưu, tìm hiểu môi trường đầu tư, kết nối đối tác trong lĩnh vực tự động hóa, sản xuất thông minh, phát triển chuỗi cung ứng, ngày 4/11.
content_md:
TP HCMĐoàn doanh nghiệp Đài Loan (Trung Quốc) tổ chức buổi giao lưu, tìm hiểu môi trường đầu tư, kết nối đối tác trong lĩnh vực tự động hóa, sản xuất thông minh, phát triển chuỗi cung ứng, ngày 4/11.

Buổi gặp gỡ tổ chức tại khách sạn Rex, với sự góp mặt của Tổng hội Liên hiệp các Doanh nghiệp Khu công nghiệp Đài Loan (Trung Quốc), nhằm hỗ trợ doanh nghiệp mở rộng thị trường Đông Nam Á. Chương trình tập trung vào hoạt động tham quan doanh nghiệp, trao đổi kỹ thuật, tìm hiểu điều kiện đầu tư và kết nối nhu cầu hợp tác với các đơn vị trong nước.

Theo đại diện Tổng hội, hoạt động nằm trong kế hoạch hỗ trợ doanh nghiệp tiếp cận thị trường quốc tế, đặc biệt trong bối cảnh chuỗi cung ứng toàn cầu đang tái cơ cấu. Việt Nam được lựa chọn nhờ nền tảng sản xuất, hệ thống chuỗi cung ứng và tiềm năng phát triển thị trường.

Chương trình năm nay ưu tiên các giải pháp sản xuất thông minh, tự động hóa, tích hợp hệ thống và dịch vụ kỹ thuật. Đoàn có sự tham gia của nhiều doanh nghiệp Đài Loan như e-Excellence, Flexium Interconnect, Yomeen, Link&We, Cosmi Global, Soar Cloud System, Onexis Solution, Darwin Precisions và Systex, cùng đại diện Đại học Khoa học và Công nghệ Cao Hùng.

Thông qua giới thiệu công nghệ, sản phẩm và trao đổi nhu cầu, các đơn vị tham gia tìm kiếm cơ hội hợp tác với doanh nghiệp Việt Nam cũng như doanh nghiệp Đài Loan đang hoạt động tại đây. Những lĩnh vực được quan tâm gồm chuyển giao công nghệ, phát triển sản phẩm, ứng dụng tự động hóa và liên kết chuỗi cung ứng.

Đoàn do ông Hứa Chính Vân, Tổng hội trưởng Tổng hội Liên hiệp các Doanh nghiệp Khu công nghiệp Đài Loan, dẫn đầu. Hoạt động tiếp nối chương trình giao lưu với cộng đồng doanh nghiệp tại Việt Nam được triển khai từ năm 2025.

Trong khuôn khổ chuyến công tác, Tổng hội dự kiến ký biên bản ghi nhớ hợp tác với Tổng hội Thương mại Đài Loan tại Việt Nam, dưới sự chứng kiến của ông Hàn Quốc Diệu, Trưởng Văn phòng Kinh tế và Văn hóa Đài Bắc tại TP HCM. Thỏa thuận hướng đến xây dựng cơ chế trao đổi thông tin thị trường, kết nối kỹ thuật và tìm kiếm cơ hội kinh doanh giữa các doanh nghiệp hai bên. Qua đó, các đơn vị có thể duy trì liên lạc và phát triển quan hệ hợp tác sau chương trình giao lưu.

Theo ông Hứa Chính Vân, doanh nghiệp khi mở rộng ra nước ngoài không chỉ cần thông tin về môi trường đầu tư mà còn cần đối tác và mạng lưới hỗ trợ lâu dài. "Điều doanh nghiệp thực sự cần là mạng lưới hợp tác có thể vận hành lâu dài và đầu mối kết nối kỹ thuật", ông nói.

Ông cho biết việc ký kết biên bản ghi nhớ được kỳ vọng giúp kết nối năng lực công nghệ của doanh nghiệp tại Đài Loan với nhu cầu sản xuất tại Việt Nam, từng bước hình thành cơ chế trao đổi thường xuyên và thúc đẩy hợp tác kinh doanh.

Chương trình gặp gỡ còn có sự hỗ trợ của Cục Quản lý Khu công nghiệp thuộc Bộ Kinh tế Đài Loan và Trung tâm Nghiên cứu và Phát triển Công nghiệp Kim loại. Các đơn vị này tham gia hỗ trợ kết nối nguồn lực, triển khai hoạt động giao lưu và phát triển hợp tác quốc tế cho doanh nghiệp.

Thời gian tới, Tổng hội dự kiến tiếp tục phối hợp các cơ quan, hiệp hội và tổ chức kỹ thuật để hỗ trợ doanh nghiệp trong khu công nghiệp mở rộng hoạt động ra nước ngoài. Trọng tâm là kết nối đối tác, trao đổi công nghệ và phát triển mạng lưới hợp tác trong lĩnh vực sản xuất thông minh.

title: Vì sao doanh nghiệp Việt khó huy động vốn ngoại?
description: Nhà đầu tư nước ngoài sẵn sàng giải ngân, nhưng hầu hết doanh nghiệp trong nước chưa đáp ứng tiêu chí quản trị, tài chính kế toán, xếp hạng tín nhiệm… để tiếp cận dòng vốn ngoại.
content_md:
Nhà đầu tư nước ngoài sẵn sàng giải ngân, nhưng hầu hết doanh nghiệp trong nước chưa đáp ứng tiêu chí quản trị, tài chính kế toán, xếp hạng tín nhiệm… để tiếp cận dòng vốn ngoại.

Theo PGS. TS Nguyễn Hữu Huân, Phó chủ tịch Cơ quan điều hành Trung tâm Tài chính quốc tế Việt Nam tại TP HCM (VIFC-HCMC), các định chế tài chính quốc tế rất muốn đầu tư vào Việt Nam. Song, mức độ đáp ứng tiêu chuẩn quốc tế của doanh nghiệp trong nước rất thấp. Hiện chỉ có tổ chức kinh tế đầu ngành, nhất là ngân hàng, đủ điều kiện huy động vốn quốc tế, còn doanh nghiệp quy mô vừa và nhỏ gần như không thể tiếp cận.

"Nhà đầu tư nước ngoài không thiếu tiền, chỉ có chúng ta đang thiếu doanh nghiệp và dự án đạt chuẩn để huy động vốn từ họ", ông Huân nói tại *Diễn đàn An ninh tài chính số Việt Nam* sáng 6/11.

Việc doanh nghiệp khó tiếp cận vốn ngoại đặt ra thách thức lớn, bởi nền kinh tế ước tính cần huy động khoảng 1.500 tỷ USD trong giai đoạn 2026-2030 để phát triển. Phần lớn nhu cầu này đang phụ thuộc vào tín dụng ngân hàng.

Ông Nguyễn Hữu Hiệu, Tổng giám đốc FiinGroup, cho rằng tích lũy trong nước sẽ không đủ đáp ứng nhu cầu vốn ngày càng lớn. Do đó, nền kinh tế cần tìm những kênh dẫn vốn mới. Huy động từ các tổ chức nước ngoài, gồm vay hợp vốn và phát hành trái phiếu, được kỳ vọng là kênh bù đắp quan trọng.

Theo thống kê của FiinGroup, 9 tháng đầu năm các tổ chức kinh tế trong nước đã huy động 24 khoản vay ngoại tệ, tổng giá trị 9,2 tỷ USD. Các ngân hàng đóng góp 12 thương vụ, chiếm tới 68% giá trị, tức khoảng 6,3 tỷ USD. Nhóm phi ngân hàng mới vay được khoảng 3 tỷ USD từ nước ngoài.

Các chuyên gia cho rằng, doanh nghiệp nhỏ và vừa - nhóm chiếm tới 98% số doanh nghiệp - tiếp cận vốn ngân hàng nội địa còn khó, nên vay vốn hay phát hành trái phiếu quốc tế gần như là điều không thể. Để đạt chuẩn huy động vốn quốc tế, doanh nghiệp phải có khung quản trị và tài chính theo tiêu chuẩn quốc tế, đồng thời được xếp hạng tín nhiệm. Điều này đòi hỏi họ phải chuẩn bị, đầu tư chi phí và nguồn lực trong thời gian rất dài mới đáp ứng.

"Nhà đầu tư quốc tế thường yêu cầu doanh nghiệp được một trong 4 hãng kiểm toán lớn (Big4) kiểm toán và lập báo cáo theo chuẩn mực IFRS thay vì chỉ dùng chuẩn kế toán Việt Nam", ông Hiệu nêu ví dụ.

Ngay cả khi đáp ứng đủ tiêu chuẩn, doanh nghiệp và ngân hàng Việt vẫn phải huy động với chi phí cao. Ông Quản Trọng Thành, Giám đốc khối Phân tích, chứng khoán Maybank, cho biết lãi suất vay nước ngoài hiện ở mức 6-8% một năm. Nếu cộng chi phí hoán đổi ngoại tệ (swap), mức này lên tới 8-9%. Trong khi đó, tại Philippines - quốc gia đã đạt hạng tín nhiệm Đầu tư, lãi suất huy động vốn quốc tế chỉ khoảng 4,5-5%.

"Điều kiện tiên quyết là nâng xếp hạng tín nhiệm quốc gia lên 'đầu tư' (Investment Grade). Điều này sẽ mở ra kênh tiếp cận vốn tốt hơn và chi phí thấp hơn cho doanh nghiệp", Phó chủ tịch VIFC-HCMC nói.

Theo ông, xếp hạng tín nhiệm quốc gia là "trần" cho xếp hạng doanh nghiệp, tức doanh nghiệp hiện nay không được xếp hạng cao hơn tín nhiệm quốc gia. Khi xếp hạng quốc gia được nâng lên, trần của doanh nghiệp cũng tăng theo, qua đó giảm chi phí huy động vốn rất nhiều.

Đồng quan điểm, chuyên gia của Chứng khoán Maybank ước tính nếu Việt Nam đạt hạng đầu tư (Investment Grade), chi phí vay nước ngoài có thể giảm về 5-6%. Khi vốn ngoại giá rẻ chảy vào, mặt bằng lãi suất trong nước cũng sẽ hạ nhiệt và ổn định hơn.

Để làm được việc này, ông Thành đề xuất Chính phủ thành lập ban chuyên trách nâng hạng tín nhiệm quốc gia. Ban này sẽ hoạt động như bộ phận quan hệ nhà đầu tư (IR) của quốc gia, làm việc trực tiếp với S&P, Moody’s, Fitch và các định chế quốc tế để cung cấp thông tin minh bạch, chính xác.

Với các dự án hạ tầng siêu lớn và dài hạn, ông cho rằng Nhà nước nên đứng ra dẫn dắt, vì đây là chủ thể huy động vốn rẻ nhất với mức lãi suất khoảng 4-5% cho sản phẩm trái phiếu chính phủ. Sau đó, Nhà nước tái cấp vốn cho các dự án chiến lược.

Song song với cải thiện xếp hạng tín nhiệm quốc gia, các chuyên gia cũng kiến nghị mở thêm kênh huy động. Theo ông Huân, TP HCM sắp triển khai các đợt phát hành trái phiếu quốc tế bằng ngoại tệ đầu tiên của một chính quyền địa phương tại Việt Nam, dành cho các dự án hạ tầng trọng điểm. Sau đó, VIFC sẽ xây dựng kênh phát hành trái phiếu quốc tế riêng cho doanh nghiệp với cơ chế đặc thù, giúp dòng tiền được hấp thụ nhanh hơn và việc kiểm soát ngoại hối thuận lợi hơn.
topic: Vì sao doanh nghiệp Việt khó huy động vốn ngoại
summary: Nhà đầu tư nước ngoài sẵn sàng giải ngân, nhưng hầu hết doanh nghiệp trong nước chưa đáp ứng tiêu chí quản trị, tài chính kế toán, xếp hạng tín nhiệm… để tiếp cận dòng vốn ngoại.

title: Vietnam's industrial parks must evolve to attract global tech giants
content_md:
Vietnam's industrial parks can no longer limit themselves to providing manufacturing space. Instead, they must evolve into integrated ecosystems that combine technology, innovation, logistics, green energy and a highly skilled workforce to attract high-value foreign investment.

That was the central message at the Vietnam Industrial Park Summit 2026, an annual international conference and exhibition held in Hai Phong on July 10 under the theme "Developing Vietnam's industrial parks in line with national industrial growth objectives."

As the global economy undergoes rapid change, marked by intensifying strategic competition, expanding trade protectionism, geopolitical tensions and the continued restructuring of global supply chains, Vietnam's industrial sector faces the dual challenge of sustaining growth while improving its competitiveness.

During the first half of 2026, the country's industrial sector continued to post solid performance, with the Industrial Production Index (IIP) rising 10.8% year-on-year. Manufacturing remained the primary growth engine, expanding 11.4% over the same period.

However, uneven growth among provinces, rising demands for energy security, infrastructure development, high-quality FDI and the transition toward greener, more sustainable production models are creating new challenges for Vietnam's industrial park system.

The summit brought together policymakers, local authorities, industrial park developers, investors, manufacturers and technology providers to identify new growth drivers for the country's industrial parks.

**Industrial parks must become innovation ecosystems**

Opening the conference, Nguyen Van Khoi, chairman of the Vietnam Association of Realtors and a member of the Prime Minister's Advisory Council on Administrative Procedure Reform, said the world is undergoing profound geopolitical, economic and technological changes.

Global supply chains are being restructured, while investment relocation, green development, digital transformation, AI and the circular economy are reshaping industrial development models.

"For Vietnam, these changes present both tremendous opportunities and significant challenges," he said. "If we want industry to grow rapidly, we must first build a modern industrial park system. If we want to attract the world's leading technology companies, we need development platforms that match their expectations. And if we want to strengthen national competitiveness, industrial parks cannot simply lease land. They must become high-quality ecosystems for manufacturing, innovation and services."

Khoi said many industrial parks still follow traditional development models. Logistics infrastructure remains fragmented, connections with urban areas are limited, and housing and social amenities for workers and professionals fall short of demand.

Meanwhile, progress in digital and green transformation has been slow, and support services for investors remain inconsistent.

He also highlighted unresolved issues involving land availability, site clearance, land prices and investment procedures.

According to Khoi, Vietnam must shift from the traditional model of industrial parks providing production space to modern industrial ecosystems.

"A successful industrial park is more than a collection of factories. It should include logistics centers, digital infrastructure, research and innovation hubs, housing for workers and professionals, educational, healthcare, commercial and cultural facilities, along with a green, safe and sustainable living environment," he said.

He added that next-generation industrial parks should be managed through digital data and equipped with AI, the Internet of Things, big data and intelligent management platforms to improve operational efficiency, reduce energy consumption, lower costs and enhance competitiveness.

**Next-generation industrial parks underpin industrial growth**

Speaking at the conference, Nguyen Duc Hien, deputy head of the Central Policy and Strategy Commission, said Vietnam aims to achieve double-digit economic growth and become a developing country with a modern industrial base by 2030.

Achieving that goal requires industry to remain the primary driver of economic growth through a new development model built on science, technology, innovation, high value-added production, green and digital transformation, and deeper integration into global value chains.

According to Hien, this requires industrial parks and economic zones to be fundamentally repositioned in terms of their functions, development models and investment quality.

"Vietnam's industrial parks cannot simply serve as manufacturing sites or infrastructure providers. They must become modern industrial ecosystems where innovation, AI-powered digital technologies and high-quality human resources converge," he said.

He added that next-generation industrial parks will provide the foundation for developing innovation clusters, boosting productivity, strengthening competitiveness and improving the resilience of Vietnam's economy while directly supporting national industrial growth.

**Building greener and smarter industrial parks**

Tran Van Quan, vice chairman of the Hai Phong People's Committee, said industrial parks and economic zones have long been central to Vietnam's industrialization and efforts to attract foreign investment into manufacturing.

He noted that 70% to 80% of newly registered FDI in manufacturing is concentrated in industrial parks and economic zones.

Foreign-invested enterprises operating in these zones contribute around 20% of Vietnam's GDP, account for more than 70% of national exports, and provide direct employment for nearly 3.83 million workers.

"These figures clearly demonstrate the role of industrial parks as a driving force behind industrial growth and national competitiveness," Quan said.

As global supply chains continue to diversify, he added, Vietnam is emerging as a preferred destination for high-tech investment.

The semiconductor sector alone has attracted more than US$14 billion across over 240 projects, while new investment is also flowing into data centers, AI and renewable energy.

Investors from South Korea, Japan, Singapore, China, the United States and Europe continue to view Vietnam's industrial parks as strategic locations within regional and global supply chains.

Quan said that during the 2026 - 2030 period, as Vietnam targets annual GDP growth of at least 10%, industrial parks must continue upgrading their planning, infrastructure, green and digital transformation capabilities while strengthening their capacity to attract projects in high technology, semiconductors and innovation.

Conference presentations also focused on developing industrial parks for a new era of economic growth, renewable energy zones, industrial park planning following administrative boundary changes and building national spatial data platforms to support smart industrial parks.

Experts discussed international standards for industrial parks, integrated digital infrastructure, energy optimization through energy management systems (EMS), data-driven smart governance and cybersecurity for critical infrastructure.

The discussions concluded with broad agreement that Vietnam's industrial parks must shift their focus from expanding in number to improving quality and efficiency while strengthening links between foreign-invested and domestic enterprises.

Such a transformation, participants said, is essential to building modern, green and sustainable industrial ecosystems capable of attracting the next generation of global investment.
topic: Khu công nghiệp phải nâng cấp để thu hút các tập đoàn công nghệ toàn cầu
summary: Tại Vietnam Industrial Park Summit 2026 ở Hải Phòng, các diễn giả cho rằng khu công nghiệp cần chuyển thành hệ sinh thái tích hợp công nghệ, logistics, năng lượng xanh và nhân lực chất lượng cao để thu hút FDI giá trị cao.
Nửa đầu năm 2026, chỉ số sản xuất công nghiệp (IIP) tăng 10,8% so với cùng kỳ, ngành chế biến, chế tạo tăng 11,4%.
Theo Phó Chủ tịch UBND Hải Phòng Trần Văn Quân, 70% đến 80% vốn FDI đăng ký mới vào sản xuất tập trung ở khu công nghiệp và khu kinh tế.
Doanh nghiệp FDI trong các khu này đóng góp khoảng 20% GDP, hơn 70% xuất khẩu và gần 3,83 triệu việc làm trực tiếp.
Ngành bán dẫn đã thu hút hơn 14 tỷ USD với hơn 240 dự án.
Việt Nam đặt mục tiêu tăng trưởng GDP bình quân tối thiểu 10% mỗi năm giai đoạn 2026-2030.
analysis: Nhận định: Xu hướng khu công nghiệp nâng cấp để hút FDI giá trị cao, nhất là bán dẫn, có thể làm tăng nhu cầu vốn đầu tư hạ tầng, tín dụng doanh nghiệp FDI và dịch vụ tài khoản, ngoại hối. Đây là diễn biến trung hạn, tác động tới ngân hàng gián tiếp.

title: Boway Alloy to invest $51 mln in northern Vietnam plant expansion
content_md:
China's Ningbo Boway Alloy Materials Co. plans to invest CNY335 million ($50.9 million) to expand its functional materials manufacturing facility in northern Vietnam, further strengthening its industrial presence in the country.

The project will be implemented through its wholly owned subsidiary, Bedra Vietnam Alloy Materials Co., at Hoa Phu Industrial Park in Bac Ninh city. The existing facility covers 10 hectares.

According to Boway Alloy’s filing with the Shanghai Stock Exchange on October 28, the expansion will use the Vietnam subsidiary's existing land and factory buildings.

The company plans to install around 103 pieces of production and supporting equipment, including automated alloying systems, extrusion presses, heavy-duty hydraulic drawing machines, and automated packaging lines, thus raising annual production capacity of 35,000 tons.

Construction is expected to take 18 months, with the expanded facility targeted to begin operations in June 2028. The project remains subject to relevant overseas investment approvals and filing procedures in China, as well as applicable investment registration procedures in Vietnam, it added.

The Vietnam expansion is part of a broader CNY1.43 billion capital expenditure plan covering four new manufacturing facilities.

The other three projects are in China: a 35,000-ton-a-year special alloy electronic material strip facility with an estimated investment of CNY574.2 million; a high-performance ultra-thin strip plant with annual capacity of 5,000 tons, costing CNY216.16 million; and a new aluminium alloy facility designed to produce 15,000 tons annually, with an investment of CNY306.3 million.

The Chinese company said capital would be deployed in stages and linked to construction milestones. The investment figures are based on internal financial estimates, with final spending subject to actual project implementation.

On October 27, Boway also announced plans to inject up to $50 million into its Vietnamese subsidiary, potentially raising its registered capital from $50 million to $100 million. The capital increase is intended to fund the expansion and should not be treated as an additional investment on top of the CNY335 million project budget.

Bedra Vietnam generated revenue of CNY756.3 million ($113 million) in the first nine months of 2026, while net profit reached CNY45.94 million ($6.86 million), around 2.5 times its full-year 2025 profit.

The company offers more than 400 types of alloy materials for industries including automotive, railways, shipbuilding, medical equipment, electronics and 5G telecommunications. Its Asian operations comprise three manufacturing facilities with a combined area of nearly 229,000 square metres, a workforce of 848 and annual production capacity of 52,900 tons.

The bedra brand is associated with German precision-wire manufacturer Berkenhoff, founded in 1889. China's Boway Group acquired the German company in 2015 from investment firm Nexpert AG. The transaction value was not disclosed.
